Developed at FC Midtjylland, he played across Italy, Germany, France, Turkey and Spain, finishing his club career with AC Milan. long_biography.plain_text:
Simon Kjær entered FC Midtjylland's pioneering academy at fifteen after playing youth football around Horsens. The Danish centre-back moved from there to Palermo, beginning a club career that later included Wolfsburg, Lille, Fenerbahçe, Sevilla and AC Milan. His positional play and authority made him a natural organiser in defence.

Leadership became Kjær's defining international trait. He captained Denmark through major tournaments and received UEFA's President's Award for his response when Christian Eriksen collapsed during the European Championship. With 132 appearances, Kjær retired as the country's second-most-capped men's player. He now serves on FC Midtjylland's board, returning to the club where his senior career began.
